findings.title: Prior-Year Intangible Impairment Reversal Distorts Headline Profit Trajectory
findings.description: Reported trading profit dropped 31.4% from R4,218m in FY2024 to R2,892m in FY2025, and profit before tax fell 27.3% from R5,155m to R3,749m. However, FY2024 headline figures were inflated by a non-recurring R1,019m 'Intangible asset impairment reversal'. On an underlying operating basis (excluding this credit), FY2024 trading profit was R3,199m, meaning underlying trading profit fell 9.6% in FY2025 rather than 31.4%. Standard unadjusted screens miss this base distortion.

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Normalized Trading Profit / Operating Margin / Earnings Growth Comps
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust FY2024 EBIT base downward by R1,019m to establish an accurate operational baseline and measure true underlying margin deterioration.

findings.title: Total Borrowings Shifted to Short-Term Debt Alongside Net Negative Cash Position
findings.description: All long-term debt has rolled into current liabilities or matured: non-current interest-bearing borrowings dropped to R0 (FY2024: R268m), while current interest-bearing borrowings rose to R1,479m (FY2024: R1,208m). Combined with a bank overdraft of R975m, the Group faces R2,454m of debt obligations due within 12 months against cash and cash equivalents of R964m, leaving net cash and cash equivalents at -R11m. This elevates near-term refinancing and interest rate risks.

findings.title: Substantial Credit Delinquency Risk and ECL Weight on Operating Profit
findings.description: The Key Audit Matter reveals that across the active trade receivables portfolio (R6,448m) and charged-off portfolio (R543m), total expected credit loss (ECL) allowances stand at R1,739m (R1,339m + R400m), representing ~25% of gross receivables. Furthermore, total trade receivable costs consumed R1,260m (including R1,164m net bad debt and ECL provisions), absorbing 43.6% of trading profit (R2,892m). High dependence on forward-looking macroeconomic overlay models leaves earnings vulnerable to South African credit deterioration.
findings.source_section: Independent Auditor's Report - Key Audit Matter
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: As at 29 June 2025 the Group’s trade receivables active portfolio amounted to R6 448 million, against which an ECL allowance of R1 339 million has been raised. The “charged-off” trade receivables portfolio... amounted to R543 million, against which an ECL allowance of R400 million was raised.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Credit Loss Ratio / Bad Debt Allowance / Operating Margin Sensitivity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Review Note 11 and Note 27.5 to evaluate active vs charged-off roll rates, write-off thresholds, and sensitivity of the economic overlay models to rising credit defaults.

findings.title: Failure of Expected South African Consumer Rebound and GNU Dividend
findings.description: Management highlights that the widely expected consumer stimulus in South Africa following the May 2024 elections (formation of the GNU and the implementation of the two-pot retirement savings withdrawals) failed to materialize due to internal coalition frictions and geopolitical/tariff uncertainties. Meanwhile, UK consumer spending remains constrained by real disposable income declines since 2021, directly challenging bullish cyclical recovery forecasts.

findings.description: Subsidiary Truworths Ltd passed a special resolution granting financial assistance to the holding company and Truworths Trading (Pty) Ltd for share acquisitions, as well as authorising financial assistance 'to certain directors of that company for housing purposes'. While executed under Section 45 of the South African Companies Act, corporate lending to directors for personal housing is an unusual governance practice requiring scrutiny.

findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Corporate Governance Risk / Related Party Loan Exposure
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Examine Note 28 (Directors and employees) and Note 32 (Related party disclosures) for the outstanding balances, interest rates, and recipient identities of director housing loans.

findings.title: Inventory Shrinkage and Write-offs Doubled Year-on-Year
findings.description: Inventory shrinkage and write-offs charged directly to cost of sales surged by 102% from R43 million in FY2024 to R87 million in FY2025. Although gross inventory allowances fell slightly from 15.3% to 13.6%, actual expensed shrinkage escalated substantially, indicating potential operational control weaknesses, store-level theft, or supply chain inventory leakage.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: During the reporting period inventory shrinkage and write offs to the value of R87 million (June 2024: R43 million) were expensed in cost of sales. Please refer to note 27.1.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross profit margin, Cost of Sales, shrinkage rate assumptions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust forecast gross margins downward to reflect elevated shrinkage levels; inquire whether shrinkage is localized to Truworths Africa or Office UK and review loss-prevention capex.

findings.title: 100% of Interest-Bearing Borrowings Classified as Current Liabilities with Heavy Reliance on Uncommitted Lines
findings.description: All of the Group's interest-bearing debt (R1,479 million) is classified under current liabilities as of FY2025 (up from R1,208 million current in FY2024, with non-current debt dropping to Rnil). The R1.2 billion revolving credit facility (fully drawn) expires 12 months after notice, and the R268 million green term loan matures in December 2025. Furthermore, net cash is negative (-R11 million) with R975 million drawn on an overdraft facility where R1.7 billion out of R2.0 billion total facilities are uncommitted.
findings.source_section: Note 16 Interest-Bearing Borrowings & Note 12 Cash and Cash Equivalents
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Current portion of interest-bearing borrowings 1,479 [2024: 1,208] ... Non-current portion of interest-bearing borrowings - [2024: 268] ... The facility expires 12 months after notice is given by the lender ... and is repayable in December 2025 ... bank overdraft forms part of a South African Rand-based general short-term banking facility of R2 billion, of which R300 million is committed and R1.7 billion is uncommitted
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Short-term liquidity risk, refinancing risk, interest rate spreads
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Verify refinancing negotiations for the R268m green loan due December 2025 and stress-test liquidity in the event the uncommitted bank overdraft facility (R1.7bn) is curtailed or called.

findings.title: Office UK Consumer Demand Deterioration and Expense Growth Pressures
findings.description: Management notes ongoing pressure on trading expense growth rates and declining sales growth for the Office UK segment during 2H2024 and FY2025 due to the UK cost-of-living crisis. While Office UK trademarks were subject to a major R1,019 million impairment reversal in FY2024 (carrying value R1,398 million in FY2025), continued macro weakness poses a risk of re-impairment.
findings.source_section: Note 5 Intangible Assets - Office UK segment
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: However, there was notable pressure on expense growth rates and a decline in sales growth rates during the second half of the 2024 reporting period, as the macro environment remains volatile and uncertain in light of the UK economic challenges and the continued decline in consumer spending on the back of the ongoing cost of living crisis.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Office UK revenue growth, operating margin, potential trademark impairment charge
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Perform sensitivity analysis on the recoverable amount of Office UK trademarks (carrying value R1,398m) using lower terminal growth and higher discount rates.

findings.title: Protracted Debtors Collection Cycle with Substantial Bad Debt Allowances
findings.description: Active debtor book collection cycle remains extremely stretched at 230 days (FY2024: 229 days), with active portfolio gross trade receivables of R6,448 million requiring an ECL allowance of R1,339 million (20.8%). Additionally, R1,154 million in new ECL allowance was raised during the year while R690 million was utilized and R427 million transferred to the charged-off portfolio, showing massive ongoing credit degradation requiring heavy provisioning.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The debtors’ days at the reporting date were 230 days (2024: 229 days). ... Expected credit loss allowances to gross active trade receivables (%) 20.8 20.3 ... Allowance raised 1,154 1,240
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Trade receivables collection period, credit loss expense, operating cash flow
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Scrutinize cash collections and credit loss provisioning rates; test sensitivity to rising interest rates on customer affordability in the SA retail segment.

findings.title: Expiration of UK HMRC IFRS 16 Tax Relief and Prior-Period Accounting Presentation Correction
findings.description: Office UK fully utilized its remaining IFRS 16 transitional tax deduction in FY2025, which will eliminate this cash tax shielding going forward. Additionally, management disclosed a restatement correcting financial assets previously presented at FVTOCI to FVTPL, pointing to past classification errors.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: As a result, the final portion of this transitional tax deduction was utilised during the 2025 financial year, with no further impact anticipated in future periods. ... In addition, we have restated assets which were incorrectly presented at fair value through other comprehensive income to assets held at fair value through profit or loss in the current financial period
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Effective tax rate, cash tax paid, P&L volatility from fair value investments
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Model a step-up in Office UK's cash tax payments for FY2026 onwards due to the lapse of the IFRS 16 HMRC tax transition allowance.

findings.title: Doubling of Current-Period Bad Debt Write-offs and Elevated Credit Allowance Coverage
findings.description: While total trade receivable costs appear flat at R1,260 million (FY2024: R1,310 million), bad debt write-offs on debt originating within the current financial year surged by 94.0% to R355 million (FY2024: R183 million). This indicates rapidly deteriorating credit vintage quality. Furthermore, active portfolio Stage 3 allowance coverage increased to 67.7% (FY2024: 64.3%), and total allowance against receivables rose to 24.9% (FY2024: 24.6%).
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Inclusive of R251 million (2024: R263 million) of bad debt recoveries and debt sold, and amounts written-off of R355 million (2024: R183 million) in respect of balances arising in the current period.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Credit loss provisions, trade receivable cash conversion, operating expenses
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Stress-test customer loan book quality and raise projected credit loss assumptions for FY2026 given that newly originated debt is defaulting twice as fast as the prior year.

findings.title: Severe Operating and Trading Margin Contraction Across Both Segments
findings.description: Group trading profit dropped 31.4% from R4,218 million to R2,892 million, collapsing the trading margin from 20.4% to 13.6% and operating margin from 27.3% to 20.0%. In Truworths Africa, gross margin slipped from 54.9% to 53.6%, and trading profit fell 16.0% (trading margin compressed from 13.3% to 11.1%). In Office UK, trading profit dropped 43.2% from R2,398 million to R1,363 million (partially distorted by the non-repeat of a R1,019 million trademark impairment reversal in FY2024, but operational trading margin fell to 18.0%).
findings.evidence_quote_or_span:
Trading profit 1,529 1,363 - 2,892
... Trading margin (%) 11.1 18.0 - 13.6
Operating margin (%) 20.4 19.4 - 20.0
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: EBITDA, operating margin, segment earnings projections
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Isolate the FY2024 Office UK intangible reversal (R1,019m) to calculate clean normalized margins, and adjust forecast margins downward to reflect persistent underlying margin compression in South Africa.

findings.title: Inventory Shrinkage and Write-offs More Than Doubled
findings.description: Inventory shrinkage and write-offs charged directly to cost of sales surged 102.3% from R43 million in FY2024 to R87 million in FY2025. This sharp increase points to worsening store-level theft, supply chain slippage, or product markdown write-offs.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Shrinkage and write-offs 10 87 43
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross margin, cost of sales
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Inquire with management regarding specific stock loss hotspots, shrink-prevention initiatives, and whether supply chain transition to the new airport DC contributed to elevated leakage.

findings.title: 100% of Interest-Bearing Borrowings Due Within 12 Months
findings.description: All R1,500 million of the Group's interest-bearing debt matures within 365 days (R1,226 million within 60-89 days and R274 million within 90-365 days), compared to FY2024 when R268 million was classified as non-current. In addition, bank overdrafts of R975 million are repayable on demand. Management specifically notes that they had to obtain a formal 'letter of funding support' from principal bankers to demonstrate liquidity headroom.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span:
Interest-bearing borrowings* - - 1,226 274 - 1,500
... Management has obtained a letter of funding support issued by the Group’s principal bankers which shows that the Group qualifies for significant funding in addition to the unutilised banking facilities, based on its solid financial track record in past years.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Refinancing risk, short-term liquidity, net finance costs
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Examine banking covenants and rollover conditions on the revolving credit facilities (RCF), especially given higher interest rates and zero long-term committed bank debt beyond 12 months.

findings.title: Zero Depreciation Taken on New Distribution Centre Due to High Residual Value Assumption
findings.description: Following the completion of construction on the TDC Airport distribution centre (where TREIC capitalised R171 million in construction costs and Truworths Ltd capitalised R722 million for materials handling equipment), management did not recognize any depreciation on the building asset because the 'residual value of the building exceeds the cost thereof'.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: At the reporting date TREIC had incurred and capitalised construction and related costs in the amount of R171 million. No depreciation has been recognised as the residual value of the building exceeds the cost thereof.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Depreciation expense, operating profit, fixed asset carrying value
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Assess the sustainability of recording zero depreciation on industrial logistics buildings and verify whether the R722m materials handling equipment is being depreciated at standard accelerated rates.

findings.title: Full-Year Dividend Reduced by 8.0% Alongside Active SARS Tax Dispute Re-assessments
findings.description: Total dividend declared for FY2025 dropped to 487 cents per share (FY2024: 529 cents per share), driven by an 8.0% cut across interim (317c vs 332c) and final (170c vs 197c) distributions, reflecting lower free cash availability. Concurrently, tax disclosures reveal that Truworths Limited received revised assessments for its 2019 tax period in September 2023 and May 2024, with disallowable expenditure including interest incurred on tax disputes.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Dividends per share ... Final cash dividend - payable/paid September 170 197 ... Interim cash dividend - paid March 317 332 ... 487 529 ... The Truworths Limited operating subsidiary received revised assessments in relation to its 2019 period on 22 September 2023 and 23 May 2024.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Dividend yield, dividend payout ratio, effective tax rate, contingent tax exposure
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust forecast payout and dividend yield expectations downward and review potential contingent liabilities stemming from the SARS 2019 reassessments.

findings.title: Severe R7.72bn Downward Fair Value Revaluation of Core South African Subsidiary
findings.description: In the standalone company financial statements, management recorded an Other Comprehensive Loss of R5.81bn, driven by a massive R7.72bn (-28.8%) downward fair value adjustment on its main trading subsidiary, Truworths Ltd (carrying value falling from R26.80bn to R19.08bn). Subsidiary valuations are conducted using consensus EV/EBITDA multiples adjusted for control and marketability, signaling severe multiple de-rating and/or cash flow contraction in the South African retail operations.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span:
Shares in Truworths Ltd
Balance at the beginning of the period 26,795,961
Revaluation recognised in other comprehensive income* (7,720,626)
Balance at the reporting date 19,075,335
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Valuation multiples, subsidiary carrying value, equity value of South African retail segment
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Examine the specific EV/EBITDA multiples and underlying EBITDA projections applied in the subsidiary Level 3 fair value models to verify whether market consensus reflects a steeper operational slowdown in South Africa than captured in consolidated headlines.

findings.title: Continued Contraction in Dividend Per Share and Cash Returns to Shareholders
findings.description: Cash returns to shareholders continued their downward trajectory. The final dividend declared post-year-end for FY2025 was 170 cents per share, representing a 13.7% cut compared to the 197 cents final dividend in FY2024 (and 245 cents in FY2023). Total declared DPS fell from 529 cents in FY2024 to 487 cents in FY2025 (-7.9%), reflecting ongoing cash conservation or diminished distributable cash generation across trading units.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span:
Total dividends declared 2,099,685 [2024: 2,357,038]
The final dividend for the period ended 29 June 2025 of 170 cents per share, before deduction of dividends tax (where applicable), was declared on 28 August 2025 to shareholders registered on the record date of 19 September 2025.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Dividend yield, dividend payout ratio, terminal growth assumptions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust future dividend distribution models to incorporate the lower baseline DPS and assess free cash flow coverage against subsidiary debt service commitments.

findings.title: Unquantified Parent Guarantee Exposure for External Operating and Real Estate Debt
findings.description: Note 7 discloses that Truworths International Ltd acts as guarantor for the external borrowings of Truworths Ltd as well as K2022434602 (t/a Truworths Real Estate Investment Company, the 50% JV for the new distribution centre). While the parent balance sheet shows negligible liabilities (R11.98m), it is exposed to external credit liabilities of the operating and DC real estate entities without disclosing specific financial exposure caps in the parent note.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The company is a guarantor for the external borrowings of Truworths Ltd and K2022434602 (SOUTH AFRICA) (Pty) Ltd (t/a Truworths Real Estate Investment Company).
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Contingent liabilities, parent solvency risk, debt covenant tracking
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Cross-reference the consolidated debt schedule and real estate borrowing facilities to quantify the total guaranteed indebtedness and evaluate recourse risk to the parent.

findings.title: Substantial Intercompany Non-Cash Dividend Settlement of Buyback Debt
findings.description: Reported standalone dividend income of R3.69bn significantly overstated realized cash flow. R1.58bn of the dividend declared by Truworths Ltd was settled via non-cash set-off against intercompany debt incurred by the holding company for historical share buybacks. Actual standalone net cash flow generated from operating activities was only R0.41m.
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The amount owing to Truworths Ltd in the prior period related mainly to financial assistance provided by Truworths Ltd to the company for the purpose of share buy-backs in prior periods, and was settled in the current period through off-set against a dividend declared by Truworths Ltd on inter-company loan account.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Holding company liquidity, cash flow from dividends, buyback capacity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Verify that standalone cash flow modeling accounts for the cessation of intercompany loan offsets and does not assume recurring non-cash dividend windfalls.

findings.title: Gross Margin Contraction Driven by Cost of Sales Outpacing Revenue Growth
findings.description: Sale of merchandise grew by only 3.2% (from R20,664m to R21,323m), while cost of sales increased by 5.4% (from R9,859m to R10,389m). This led to a 100 bps deterioration in gross margin from 52.3% to 51.3%, signaling pricing pressure, higher input costs, or elevated promotional markdowns.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Statements of Comprehensive Income
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross margin, Cost of sales growth, Operating margin
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust forward gross margin assumptions down by at least 100 bps and assess whether markdown activity or freight/input cost inflation is continuing into FY2026.

findings.title: Prior Period Flattered by R1.28bn of One-Off Reversals and Non-Operating Credits
findings.description: Reported operating comparisons are severely distorted by FY2024 one-off items. FY2024 reported earnings included a R1,019m trademark impairment reversal for Office UK, R122m net right-of-use asset impairment reversal, R123m one-time operating cost reduction from consolidating charitable trusts, and R20m insurance recovery. Even after pro forma normalization removing these one-offs, FY2025 pro forma trading profit fell 1%, pro forma PBT fell 3%, and pro forma HEPS fell 4%, revealing underlying operational stagnation.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Basis of Preparation
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The Group’s prior period earnings were enhanced by the following once-off events/transactions, making the prior period reported figures less comparable to the current period (and hence the pro forma adjustments): • a trademark impairment reversal in relation to the Office UK trademark (R1 019 million); • a net right of use asset impairment reversal (R122 million)... • insurance recoveries in Office UK (R20 million)... and • a reduction in other operating costs (R123 million) resulting from the consolidation of the Group's charitable trusts for the first time.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Normalized EBITDA, Base earnings growth rate, Return on equity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Ensure base-year modeling uses pro forma normalized earnings (Pro forma 2024 PBT R3,871m / HEPS 780.8c) rather than reported IFRS figures to avoid projecting an artificial earnings rebound.

findings.title: Escalating Fixed Overheads and Financing Costs Exert Operating Leverage Headwind
findings.description: Occupancy costs expanded 7% (R1,072m to R1,145m) and finance costs surged 10% (R476m to R525m), both significantly outstripping the 3% top-line merchandise sales growth. This ongoing cost pressure compresses reported operating margin from 27.3% to 20.0% (and pro forma operating margin from 21.0% to 20.1%).
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Statements of Comprehensive Income
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Occupancy costs (1,145) ... (1,072) ... 7% ; Finance costs (525) ... (476) ... 10% ; Operating margin (%) 20.0 ... 27.3
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Operating margin, Net finance expense, Free cash flow
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Stress-test occupancy cost escalation rates and debt financing costs against low single-digit sales growth assumptions.

findings.title: Extraction Error: Trading Profit Percentage Change Mislabeled as Metric Value
findings.description: The candidate data pipeline extracted 'trading_profit: -31' from page 150. In the source table, -31 is the percentage change (-31%) of reported trading profit from FY2024 (R4,218m) to FY2025 (R2,892m), rather than the actual monetary value.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Statements of Comprehensive Income
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: trading_profit metric value
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Correct automated extractor to capture actual trading profit (R2,892m reported / R2,909m pro forma) instead of the column variance percentage.

findings.title: Substantial Institutional Divestment by Major Global and Local Asset Managers
findings.description: The register of disclosures of beneficial interests and major fund managers shows that Ninety One completely exited its >3% position (down from 8.9% / 36.2m shares in 2024 to below 3% in 2025), BlackRock exited its >3% position (down from 3.0% / 12.3m shares), Old Mutual Investment Group reduced from 8.3% to 4.6%, and Westwood Global reduced from 7.1% to 6.9%.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Cost of equity, Share price overhang / institutional demand
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Investigate reasons behind large institutional sell-offs by tier-one global and domestic institutions during the fiscal year.
